QF.id: XVI Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_54

question.text: Under the default-waterfall arrangement of a commodity clearing corporation, the Settlement Guarantee Fund (SGF) is primarily utilised to:

answer.text: Meet settlement obligations when a trading member fails to meet its settlement obligation
Decide the sequence of trading priority for orders
Determine the order in which commodities are delivered at warehouses

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM Series XVI page 161 states that the SGF is utilised, as required under the default-waterfall arrangement, when a trading member fails to meet its settlement obligation. The fund is therefore a member-default resource used by the clearing corporation to honour settlement to non-defaulting counterparties. The Trap: The SGF has nothing to do with order-execution priority, the sequencing of warehouse deliveries, or the processing of new membership applications. It is purely a settlement-default protection mechanism. Note: The exact ordering of the default waterfall (for example member margin, then SGF, then clearing corporation capital) is not specified on the pages checked; this question therefore focuses on the source-supported role of the SGF within that waterfall, not on the precise sequence.
